note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 2394 / 出力 2110 トークン

data.interpretation: The KPI asks that the road rules be followed and that road-rule violations (release deadline overruns and blocking_guard evictions) be reduced as far as possible. This maps directly to road_violations, not violation_total, which also counts late deliveries. However, road_violations is a proxy for safe, orderly road use. It can be lowered in ways that defeat the intent: rules could be loosened so that fewer events count as violations, or robots could move less or hold back deliveries. Reading 'make sure the rules are kept' as a hard zero-violation requirement is also possible. Each reading needs a different evaluation, so the human should choose.

options.label: Minimize road violations only

goals.text: Primary: reduce the number of road-rule violations (release overruns and blocking_guard evictions).
Watch: total time robots are blocked by stopped robots should not get worse.

options.note: Closest to the literal KPI. It does not protect delivery performance, so an amendment that cuts violations by slowing or suppressing deliveries, or by loosening rule definitions, could be adopted.

options.label: Minimize road violations while protecting delivery service

goals.text: Primary: reduce the number of road-rule violations.
Watch: blocked time should not increase. This catches rule loosening that hides real obstruction.
Watch: town-wide on-time deliveries should not drop.
Watch: orders left undelivered at period end should not increase.

guards.text: No company's on-time rate may fall below 80% after the amendment. This prevents violations being cut by sacrificing one company's service. The threshold is a placeholder and should be set from the measured baseline.

options.note: Recommended. Improvement is still measured by road_violations, but the amendment cannot pass by hiding obstruction or by sacrificing deliveries. The 0.8 guard value is a placeholder and should be replaced with the current baseline value.

options.label: Zero road violations as a hard requirement

goals.text: Primary: drive road-rule violations down, with zero as the required end state.
Watch: blocked time should not increase.
Watch: on-time deliveries should not drop.

guards.text: After the amendment there must be no road-rule violations at all.

options.note: Reads 'make sure the road rules are kept' as an absolute requirement. This may reject every realistic amendment if zero is not reachable in one step, and it creates strong pressure to loosen the rules themselves.

concerns: road_violations is a proxy. Because the road rules themselves (ROAD_USE) can be amended, an amendment could lower the count by loosening release deadlines or blocking_guard conditions, without making the roads any less obstructed. Watching blocked_s helps detect this.

Violations can also be reduced by robots moving less, yielding excessively, or delaying pickups, which would hurt deliveries. The KPI says nothing about delivery service, so it is unclear whether that trade-off is acceptable.
'Make sure the road rules are kept' could mean a hard zero-violation requirement rather than 'as few as possible'. These lead to different evaluations: option 3 versus options 1 and 2.
The guard threshold in option 2 (minimum company on-time rate 0.8) is a placeholder. It should be set from the measured baseline before use.
